expects.rule: The first screen states what the product does and for whom in one headline and one supporting line, with a primary action and a secondary one (try, and talk to sales or book a demo).
A real product screenshot or live interface is visible on or just below the first screen, not only an abstract illustration.
Customer proof (logos, a named quote, a case study) appears near the top and names real companies.
Pricing information (plans, a range or typical cases) is shown and reachable from the main navigation in one click, and the navigation has no more than about seven items.
Features are grouped by the job they do for the visitor, each with a visual of the actual product.
Login and demo or sign-up links stay visible in the header on every page.
The page loads fast and does not hide its text behind animation: the headline is readable before scripts finish.

traits: Headline of 8 words or fewer on 5 of 8 sites; Relato, Parloa and Linear run longer.
The first screen holds fewer than 60 words on 7 of 8 sites and at most two buttons; Linear and Raycast show a single action or none beside the nav.
6 of 8 sites show a header login link and a demo, trial or download button; Nucleo and Raycast use Buy or Download instead.
Typefaces: 2 or 3 named families on 8 of 8; 5 of 8 pair a sans with a serif or a mono face.
The headline is set at 54 to 80px on 7 of 8 sites (Nucleo uses heavy capitals across the full width).
A real or mocked product interface is visible on the first screen on 3 of 8 (Linear, Relato, incident.io); the rest lead with art or photography.
Backgrounds: 4 of 8 are white or near-white, 3 near-black or dark; one accent colour (orange or red on 4 of 8).

sites.name: incident.io

sites.name: Speakeasy
sites.why: Light grey page (#fafafa), a boxed announcement tag in mono capitals, a two-line light serif headline (Tobias) at left, a paragraph of four lines, and a large ASCII-character artwork at right. Nav has a Talk to us button with a gradient edge.

sites.name: Linear
sites.why: Near-black page (#08090a), a left-aligned two-line headline in Inter at 64px, a two-line subhead, then a real issue view (sidebar, activity, properties) starting at the bottom edge. Nav: Product, Resources, Customers, Pricing, Now, Contact, Log in, Sign up.
sites.recognition: Cited as a best-in-class developer-facing site in Veza Digital article, 2026-09-03

avoid: A hero with a gradient blob or abstract 3D shape and no view of the product.
Three identical feature cards with an icon, a two-word title and one line of text, repeated down the page.
A headline made of buzzwords ("supercharge", "unlock", "seamless") that does not say what the product does.
Fake or anonymous testimonials and logo walls of companies that are not customers.
Pricing hidden behind a contact form with no range, number or plan names.
Text that appears only after a scroll animation runs, so the page looks empty without scripts or with reduced motion.
